proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30 2013`, PDF pages 81-82 of the FY2013 annual town report (printed pages 77-78). TWO LANDSCAPE PAGES, ONE TABLE, printed sideways with no text layer; both were rotated upright and read off their own 400 dpi bitmaps. The fiscal years run ACROSS: page 81 carries `2014` to `2030` and page 82 carries `2031` to `2047` and a final `TOTAL` column. Column names read off the printed header (rule 13b.4): the row labels used here are the page's own, verbatim -- `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL`, `GRAND TOTAL INTEREST`, `TOTAL DEBT` -- and each fiscal year is a ROW of this file because that is the grain the series runs in. THIS IS A PARTIAL READ AND THAT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THIS CARD. ONLY THE THREE GRAND-TOTAL ROWS ARE TRANSCRIBED -- the town's whole debt service by year, FY2014 to FY2047, which is the series anybody would chart. THE PER-ISSUE ROWS ABOVE THEM ARE NOT READ: about ten borrowings, each printed as PRINCIPAL, INTEREST and a group total, across 34 year columns. So this file CANNOT say which bond ends in which year or what any single issue costs. That limit is already a registered row in `sources/data/money-gaps.csv` -- *What does each individual debt issue cost the town in a given year, and which of them fall off when?* -- and FY2013 belongs to it; no new gap is filed for it. THE CHECKS. (1) Each fiscal year states an identity: grand total principal plus grand total interest is total debt. 33 OF 34 YEARS CLOSE EXACTLY. (2) All three rows foot to the `TOTAL` column the table prints: principal 24,298,664 EXACTLY across 34 values, interest 7,307,840 within $1, total debt 31,187,800 within $1. THE TOLERANCE IS $1 AND HERE IS ITS DERIVATION. The schedule prints WHOLE DOLLARS over amounts that carry cents, so a printed total is the rounded sum and not the sum of the rounded parts. 34 addends; the observed maximum miss is $1 on two of the three rows. WHAT SAYS THIS IS ROUNDING AND NOT A MISREAD IS THE CONTRAST: `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL` -- bond principal, which has no cents under it -- ties to its printed TOTAL EXACTLY at 24,298,664, while the two rows that do carry cents underneath each miss by exactly $1. The tolerance was not widened to make anything pass. AND FY2024 IS ATTESTED: THE TOWN'S OWN ARITHMETIC DISAGREES WITH ITSELF. The 2024 column prints GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL 846,635 and GRAND TOTAL INTEREST 120,310, which make 966,945, against a printed TOTAL DEBT of 548,241 -- the document out by 418,704. All three digits were re-read at 400 dpi in a tight crop of that column. TWO THINGS CORROBORATE IT and neither depends on the other. First, the SAME 418,704 is the amount by which the printed TOTAL column fails the same identity: 24,298,664 + 7,307,840 = 31,606,504 against a printed TOTAL DEBT total of 31,187,800. Second, each of the three rows separately foots to its own printed TOTAL (principal exactly, the other two within the declared $1), so the defect is one cell and not a column. WHICH CELL IS WRONG IS NOT ESTABLISHED. 846,635 less 418,704 is 427,931, and 418,704 is also the figure this report prints in the 2024 column of a `TOTAL MASS WATER POLL TRUST` row higher up the page -- that is an OBSERVATION about two figures being equal, not a cause, and nothing here tests whether the principal row double-counts a trust borrowing or the total-debt row omits one. THE FY2014 REPORT PRINTS THE SAME SCHEDULE A YEAR LATER and its `MASS WATER POOL 9*` row carries a principal of 418,704 in the FY2024 column with no interest and no total beside it -- the only such row in that 156-row schedule (fy2014-p40-debt-schedule.csv). Same amount, same year, same borrowing, different document. That LOCATES the discrepancy on the Mass Water Pool 9 balloon payment; it does not say which of FY2013's two figures is right. WHAT THIS IS (CLAUDE.md rule 11): scheduled debt SERVICE on borrowings outstanding at 30 June 2013. It is not an appropriation, it excludes anything borrowed since, and the figures are gross -- the MSBA and Mass Water Pollution Abatement Trust subsidies that pay part of some of these issues are not netted here and are not shown.

THIS IS A PARTIAL READ AND THAT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THIS CARD. ONLY THE THREE GRAND-TOTAL ROWS ARE TRANSCRIBED -- the town's whole debt service by year, FY2014 to FY2047, which is the series anybody would chart. THE PER-ISSUE ROWS ABOVE THEM ARE NOT READ: about ten borrowings, each printed as PRINCIPAL, INTEREST and a group total, across 34 year columns. So this file CANNOT say which bond ends in which year or what any single issue costs. That limit is already a registered row in `sources/data/money-gaps.csv` -- *What does each individual debt issue cost the town in a given year, and which of them fall off when?* -- and FY2013 belongs to it; no new gap is filed for it. THE CHECKS. (1) Each fiscal year states an identity: grand total principal plus grand total interest is total debt. 33 OF 34 YEARS CLOSE EXACTLY. (2) All three rows foot to the `TOTAL` column the table prints: principal 24,298,664 EXACTLY across 34 values, interest 7,307,840 within $1, total debt 31,187,800 within $1. THE TOLERANCE IS $1 AND HERE IS ITS DERIVATION. The schedule prints WHOLE DOLLARS over amounts that carry cents, so a printed total is the rounded sum and not the sum of the rounded parts. 34 addends; the observed maximum miss is $1 on two of the three rows. WHAT SAYS THIS IS ROUNDING AND NOT A MISREAD IS THE CONTRAST: `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL` -- bond principal, which has no cents under it -- ties to its printed TOTAL EXACTLY at 24,298,664, while the two rows that do carry cents underneath each miss by exactly $1. The tolerance was not widened to make anything pass. AND FY2024 IS ATTESTED: THE TOWN'S OWN ARITHMETIC DISAGREES WITH ITSELF. The 2024 column prints GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL 846,635 and GRAND TOTAL INTEREST 120,310, which make 966,945, against a printed TOTAL DEBT of 548,241 -- the document out by 418,704. All three digits were re-read at 400 dpi in a tight crop of that column. TWO THINGS CORROBORATE IT and neither depends on the other. First, the SAME 418,704 is the amount by which the printed TOTAL column fails the same identity: 24,298,664 + 7,307,840 = 31,606,504 against a printed TOTAL DEBT total of 31,187,800. Second, each of the three rows separately foots to its own printed TOTAL (principal exactly, the other two within the declared $1), so the defect is one cell and not a column. WHICH CELL IS WRONG IS NOT ESTABLISHED. 846,635 less 418,704 is 427,931, and 418,704 is also the figure this report prints in the 2024 column of a `TOTAL MASS WATER POLL TRUST` row higher up the page -- that is an OBSERVATION about two figures being equal, not a cause, and nothing here tests whether the principal row double-counts a trust borrowing or the total-debt row omits one. THE FY2014 REPORT PRINTS THE SAME SCHEDULE A YEAR LATER and its `MASS WATER POOL 9*` row carries a principal of 418,704 in the FY2024 column with no interest and no total beside it -- the only such row in that 156-row schedule (fy2014-p40-debt-schedule.csv). Same amount, same year, same borrowing, different document. That LOCATES the discrepancy on the Mass Water Pool 9 balloon payment; it does not say which of FY2013's two figures is right. WHAT THIS IS (CLAUDE.md rule 11): scheduled debt SERVICE on borrowings outstanding at 30 June 2013. It is not an appropriation, it excludes anything borrowed since, and the figures are gross -- the MSBA and Mass Water Pollution Abatement Trust subsidies that pay part of some of these issues are not netted here and are not shown.
